bottom_line: In ONTARGET, telmisartan was noninferior to ramipril for the primary composite outcome (relative risk, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94 to 1.09).
implications: Based on the reported relative risk and confidence interval, telmisartan and ramipril produced similar rates of the primary composite outcome (16.7% vs. 16.5%; relative risk, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.94 to 1.09), while combination therapy did not improve the primary outcome versus ramipril (16.3% vs. 16.5%; relative risk, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.07) and had higher rates of renal impairment and hypotensive symptoms as reported.

major_points.text: Patients underwent double-blind randomization to ramipril, telmisartan, or the combination after a single-blind run-in period.
major_points.quote: After a 3-week, single-blind run-in period, patients underwent double-blind random- ization, with 8576 assigned to receive 10 mg of ramipril per day, 8542 assigned to receive 80 mg of telmisartan per day, and 8502 assigned to receive both drugs

major_points.text: The primary composite outcome was death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary composite outcome was death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.

major_points.text: At a median follow-up of 56 months, the primary outcome occurred at similar rates with telmisartan and ramipril.
major_points.quote: At a median follow-up of 56 months, the pri- mary outcome had occurred in 1412 patients in the ramipril group (16.5%), as compared with 1423 patients in the telmisartan group (16.7%; relative risk, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94 to 1.09).

major_points.text: Combination therapy did not reduce the primary outcome versus ramipril but increased hypotensive symptoms, syncope, and renal dysfunction.
major_points.quote: In the combination-therapy group, the primary outcome occurred in 1386 patients (16.3%; relative risk, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.07); as compared with the ramipril group, there was an increased risk of hypotensive symptoms (4.8% vs. 1.7%, P<0.001), syncope

major_points.text: Telmisartan had lower rates of cough and angioedema than ramipril, with higher hypotensive symptoms; syncope was the same.
major_points.quote: As compared with the ramipril group, the telmisartan group had lower rates of cough (1.1% vs. 4.2%, P<0.001) and angio- edema (0.1% vs. 0.3%, P = 0.01) and a higher rate of hypotensive symptoms (2.6% vs. 1.7%, P<0.001); the rate of syncope was the same

major_points.text: The primary analysis included all randomized patients and used a time-to-event approach.
major_points.quote: The primary analysis used a time-to-event ap- proach, counting the first occurrence of any com- ponent of the composite outcome, and includ­ed all randomized patients.

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome occurred in 1412 (16.5%) with ramipril and 1423 (16.7%) with telmisartan.
absolute_effects.quote: The primary outcome occurred in 1412 patients (16.5%) in the ramipril group, in 1423 patients (16.7%) in the telmisartan group

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome occurred in 1386 (16.3%) with combination therapy and 1412 (16.5%) with ramipril.
absolute_effects.quote: The primary outcome occurred in 1412 patients (16.5%) in the ramipril group, in 1423 patients (16.7%) in the telmisartan group, and in 1386 pa- tients (16.3%) in the combination-therapy group

absolute_effects.text: Renal impairment occurred in 871 (10.2%) with ramipril and 1148 (13.5%) with combination therapy.
Death from any cause occurred in 1014 (11.8%) with ramipril and 989 (11.6%) with telmisartan.

subgroups.text: Consistency of treatment effects in prespecified subgroups was explored by Cox regression with tests for interaction.
subgroups.quote: Consistency of treatment effects in prespecified sub- groups was explored by the Cox regression model, with tests for interaction.16,17

subgroups.text: Comparisons of key subgroups showed similar results between ramipril and telmisartan and between ramipril and combination therapy.
subgroups.quote: Comparisons of key subgroups showed similar results between the ramipril group and the telmi­ sartan group (Fig. 3A) and between the ramipril group and the combination-therapy group (Fig. 3B).

harms.text: Telmisartan had lower cough and angioedema but higher hypotensive symptoms than ramipril; syncope rate was the same.
harms.quote: the telmisartan group had lower rates of cough (1.1% vs. 4.2%, P<0.001) and angio- edema (0.1% vs. 0.3%, P = 0.01) and a higher rate of hypotensive symptoms (2.6% vs. 1.7%, P<0.001); the rate of syncope was the same

harms.text: Combination therapy increased hypotensive symptoms, syncope, and renal dysfunction compared with ramipril.
harms.quote: as compared with the ramipril group, there was an increased risk of hypotensive symptoms (4.8% vs. 1.7%, P<0.001), syncope (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.03), and renal dysfunction (13.5% vs. 10.2%, P<0.001).

harms.text: Total discontinuations were higher with combination therapy than ramipril.
Cough-related discontinuation was lower with telmisartan than ramipril.
Renal impairment-related discontinuation was higher with combination therapy than ramipril.

inclusion_criteria.text: Patients with coronary, peripheral, or cerebrovascular disease or diabetes with end-organ damage were enrolled.
inclusion_criteria.quote: We enrolled patients with coronary, periph- eral, or cerebrovascular disease or diabetes with end-organ damage.

exclusion_criteria.text: Patients who could not tolerate ACE inhibitors were assigned to a parallel trial.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who could not toler- ate ACE inhibitors were randomly assigned to receive either telmisartan or placebo in a parallel trial.

analysis_methods.text: Three formal interim analyses were conducted when 25%, 50%, and 75% of events accrued.
analysis_methods.quote: three formal interim anal- yses were conducted when 25%, 50%, and 75% of the events accrued.
A total of 25,620 patients underwent random- ization

analysis_methods.text: Planned sample size and follow-up provided power for superiority and noninferiority under stated hazard ratios.
analysis_methods.quote: The original planned sample size of 7800 patients who were followed for a mean of 4.5 years provided a power of 93% for the supe- riority hypothesis, if the hazard ratio was 0.87. For noninferiority, the expected power was 89%, for a hazard ratio of 1.00.

analysis_methods.text: Consistency of treatment effects in prespecified subgroups was explored by Cox regression with tests for interaction.
analysis_methods.quote: Consistency of treatment effects in prespecified sub- groups was explored by the Cox regression model, with tests for interaction.16,17

analysis_methods.text: Primary analysis included all randomized patients in a time-to-event approach counting first occurrence of any component.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary analysis used a time-to-event ap- proach, counting the first occurrence of any com- ponent of the composite outcome, and includ­ed all randomized patients.

trial_conduct.text: Protocol was approved by regulatory authorities and the ethics review committee at each participating institution.
trial_conduct.quote: The protocol was approved by regu- latory authorities and the ethics review commit- tee at each participating institution.
After written informed consent was obtained

trial_conduct.text: Main outcomes were adjudicated centrally by a committee unaware of study-group assignments using standard criteria.
trial_conduct.quote: All main study outcomes (death according to any cause, myocardial infarction, stroke, and hos- pitalization for heart failure) were adjudicated by a central committee whose members were un- aware of study-group assignments, with the use of standard criteria.14

trial_conduct.text: All serious adverse events were reviewed by an independent data and safety monitoring board.
trial_conduct.quote: All serious adverse events were reviewed by an independent data and safety monitoring board.

trial_conduct.text: A modified Haybittle–Peto approach guided interim decisions with specified SD boundaries for efficacy and safety.
trial_conduct.quote: A modified Haybittle–Peto approach15 guided decisions (i.e., a boundary of 4 SD in the first half of the trial and 3 SD in the second half for efficacy; for safety, if boundaries of 3 SD and 2 SD, respectively, were crossed

criticisms.quote: cause we used an active run-in phase that selected patients for randomization only if they tolerated both medications.
